summary.intent: Close out stale umbrella tracking issues, audit all open comp:engine issues for validity, and — after the user decided the blueprint/CONTEXT.md commit history should be fully backed by ADRs before moving the decision corpus into the main repo — perform an exhaustive history audit, independently verify challenged findings, author and land all 23 missing ADRs, reword the blueprint to match them, and finally plan the ADR repo migration.
summary.outcome: Closed #635/#991/#992 and rescoped six comp:engine issue bodies; ran a full multi-pass audit of 116 commits touching the blueprint/CONTEXT.md producing 325 classified rule rows; drafted, reviewed, and merged 23 new ADRs (0029-0051) plus a status-flip PR and 12 amendment PRs/comments in cipher-box-next; landed three blueprint-reword PRs and one comment-citation chore PR in cipher-box; filed 9+ defect issues discovered along the way; and produced an accepted migration plan (flat copy of decisions/ into cipher-box, archive cipher-box-next) pending execution.

repo: Agent-authored GitHub comments/issue bodies posted under the owner's account (FSM1) are NOT proof the owner decided anything — establish an explicit ownership test before trusting 'Decision:' comments as authoritative

The user's standing rule (recorded in memory): an in-session record of the owner making a choice counts as an owner decision, and the map #813 resolution comments are owner-approved even though agent-templated
tracker-refs CI gate exempts bare 1-2 digit '#NN' issue references on the assumption they can only refer to cipher-box-next; this breaks if cipher-box-next issues are ever renumbered/transferred
cipher-box allows squash-merge only, so migrating cipher-box-next's 76-commit ADR history via PR can't preserve commit history — recommend leaving history in the archived source repo instead
markdownlint in this repo refuses to lint a path outside the repo root; feed content via --stdin --config .markdownlint.json instead
worktree checkouts lack node_modules so the pre-commit lint-staged hook fails; format/lint by hand then commit --no-verify
cipher-box-next has no CI and no lint config, unlike cipher-box

The 'Entire' commit-hook tool only appends an Entire-Checkpoint trailer for a live top-level session with untracked changes — it does not track sub-agent sessions, so squashing via sub-agent drops the trailer and it must be restored by hand from the reflog/checkpoint store
GitHub nested sub-agent task-notification results route to the top-level orchestrator, not to the spawning parent agent — must be manually forwarded via SendMessage or the parent stalls waiting
gh commands must be run as `env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh ...` in this environment
PR bodies use `@coderabbitai ignore` for docs-only/chore PRs to skip CodeRabbit's review slot; pushing to an already-ready PR can still spend a CodeRabbit slot
workflow: For large fan-out audits, split by file/topic ownership across parallel read-only sub-agents, then run an independent second-pass 'challenge' investigation with fresh agents (not the original raters) on contested items before trusting the verdicts
Use a writer→independent reviewer→writer-revises→orchestrator-opens-PR pipeline per artifact (here, per ADR) so review findings are fixed before anything is merged

When an agent's fix touches something outside its assigned scope (e.g. a residual affecting an already-open PR), have the orchestrator explicitly amend that other PR rather than letting drift accumulate

Maintain a running scratch directory (~/.claude/scratch/<topic>/) with versioned summary docs (v1, v2, v3...) as successive investigation passes refine the same dataset, so nothing is silently overwritten

When diagramming architecture trade-offs for a non-technical explanation, use the archify skill to produce interactive HTML diagrams with delivered/visual-checked screenshots rather than describing purely in prose

Before large text-rewrite fan-outs (blueprint reword), run extraction agents (pull exact quote+replacement per source) separately from apply agents (which perform the literal edits) to keep provenance auditable

Always run an independent 'diff review' agent against the source-of-truth (the 23 ADRs) after a large multi-agent text-editing pass, since edits outside the direct diff scope can go stale (e.g. one changed sentence contradicting another untouched sentence)

friction: Nested sub-agent results were misdelivered to the orchestrator instead of their spawning parent multiple times, requiring manual SendMessage forwarding
GitHub API rate limits (both REST and GraphQL) were hit multiple times during the ~23-PR opening spree, requiring waits and a switch of the PR-opening script from GraphQL to REST
An agent's `rm *.orig.md` glob accidentally deleted other agents' sibling scratch files (harmless since GitHub retains edit history, but a near-miss)
Auditors initially used inconsistent bars for what counts as 'owner-decided' (PR-DECIDED), requiring a dedicated re-rating pass on 21+25 unrated sources
The commit-hook Entire-Checkpoint trailer was lost during a sub-agent squash and had to be manually reconstructed from the reflog
